chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Yahya ibn Ubada, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he heard him say:

A man from the Ansar died, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) observed him [and said]: 'Greenify him.' So how few are the greenified on the Day of Resurrection. He said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'And what is greenification?' He said: 'A fresh palm leaf, about the length of a forearm, is taken and placed here' - and he pointed with his hand to near his collarbone - 'wrapped with his clothes.'

key_terms.التَّخْضِير: Greenification, a ritual act of placing greenery (palm leaf) with the deceased
key_terms.الْمُتَخَضِّرِينَ: The greenified, those who performed the ritual of greenification
key_terms.جَرِيدَةٌ: A fresh palm leaf or frond
key_terms.ذِرَاعٌ: A forearm, used as a unit of measurement for length

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual of greenification (takhdir) in Shia burial practices and what is its significance?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* details the specific Sunnah of 'takhdir' (greenification), where a fresh palm frond is placed at the deceased's collarbone before shrouding, a practice attributed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his progeny). The Imam’s remark that few will perform this on the Day of Resurrection underscores its spiritual rarity and serves as a reminder of the importance of adhering to prophetic burial customs in Shia tradition.
